Laravel hops and vendor/#

This page covers what Laravel hops need from the app, and where the hop data comes from. Next: Deploying on Citadel.

rector-laravel needs Laravel's classes to recognize a model or a controller. For a Laravel hop Booster loads the app's own vendor/autoload.php when it exists, so run composer install in the app first. PHP hops never load the app's autoloader. An app with no vendor/ still gets a plan and the hops that do not need Laravel's classes.

For an Inertia/Vue app, each Laravel hop also raises the Inertia constraints the app already carries: inertiajs/inertia-laravel and @inertiajs/vue3 move to the constraint the hop data pairs with the target major (^2.0 for Laravel 11 and newer). Booster never adds a package the app does not have, and below Laravel 11 it pins nothing and says so, because the hop data carries no constraint there.

Hop data#

data/versions.json holds the version facts Booster plans against: the PHP, Laravel and PHPUnit chains, the PHP range each Laravel major supports, the PHPUnit floor each Laravel major ships, the Node floor the node-pin-24 hop writes, the Vite major and plugin pins the vite-major hop uses, and the fixed Tailwind, TypeScript and vue-tsc pins, the fixed Inertia 3 constraints and the Inertia constraint tables the front-end hops use. The file ships inside the PHAR. A new major appears in the file as soon as its feed says so; Booster offers a hop for it only once Rector ships a ruleset for it, and a plan toward a major without one stops there with a warning instead of failing.

bin/refresh-hop-data.php rewrites the file from the public feeds (Packagist for PHPUnit and Laravel, endoflife.date for Laravel's supported PHP ranges, npm for the Vite packages) plus CREED's policy for what counts as supported:

php bin/refresh-hop-data.php             # fetch the feeds, rewrite the file, print what changed
php bin/refresh-hop-data.php --check     # offline CI check: validate the shape, then compare the frozen feeds
php bin/refresh-hop-data.php --online    # compare against the live feeds without writing the file
php bin/refresh-hop-data.php --offline tests/fixtures/hop-feeds --today 2026-10-29 --dry-run

The refresh is deterministic for a given set of feeds and date, and it never touches the recipes: writing a playbook for a new hop stays human work. composer ci ends with the offline --check: it validates the file's shape against the bundled policy, then recomputes it from the frozen feeds in tests/fixtures/hop-feeds as of the file's generated_on date, so the check itself needs no network. A scheduled pipeline runs the hop data robot, bin/hop-data-bot.php, against the live feeds; when a feed moved while the file slept, the robot opens (or updates) a merge request on Booster itself with the new file, and a person merges it. MAINTAINING.md covers the token the robot needs.
